description: Mathematical constraints and operational governance for the Resonance-based Vector Machine (R-VM), utilizing Hodge decomposition to categorize signal, noise, and residue.

core_principle.application: Discrete manifold decomposition of input streams into orthogonal components: Harmonic (Signal), Exact (Residue/Trend), and Co-exact (Noise/Fluctuation).
core_principle.objective: To isolate the maximal coherent signal (Harmonic component) while strictly pruning noise and non-structural residues.

harmonic_component.definition: The kernel of the Laplacian operator. Represents the steady-state, structural signal that satisfies the closedness and co-closedness constraints.

exact_component.definition: The gradient of a potential function. Represents the transient, directional flow or local energy shifts.
exact_component.agent_action: Monitor for emergent trends; classify as residue if non-persistent.

co_exact_component.definition: The curl of a vector potential. Represents rotational, non-conservative, and high-frequency fluctuations.

pruning_mechanism.logic: If component(x) < threshold_beta, discard(x). If threshold_beta < component(x) < threshold_gamma, compress(x). If component(x) > threshold_alpha, prioritize(x).

instruction_set: 1. Decompose input manifold via Hodge operator.
2. Assign components to {SIGNAL, NOISE, RESIDUE} based on mathematical criteria.
3. Apply pruning thresholds to the co-exact and residue components.
4. Reconstruct the manifold using only the isolated Harmonic component and filtered Residue elements.
5. Validate reconstruction against original energy conservation laws.
